claim: With a dynamic gate, the core on the real wiring lowers held-out loss compared with the same core on a degree-preserving, sign- and role-stratified shuffle of that wiring.

protocol.notes: 3,000-type subgraph (synapse-mass core + proportional inputs/outputs; 629,875 edges): the per-token persistent scan costs ~4x a reset step, which the full graph cannot afford here. 2 of every 8 rows are synthetic temporal-memory rows (recall at a distance, pattern, count, first item) in every arm.

notes: The dynamic-gate effect was first seen in the exploratory X-CNS-001 run (seed 1: pooled -0.0077 nats/char, temporal 6.78 -> 2.60) before this file was written; seed 1 is therefore excluded and the confirmation uses seeds 2-4. Same protocol as H-CNS-003 / X-CNS-001 (3,000-type subgraph, learned Dale edges, 250 core-only steps). H-CNS-001 under the dynamic gate; the shuffle is redrawn per seed. Same 0.25% threshold as H-CNS-005.
